reviews.text: cozy

Love this concept of a BBS Door Game. What you’ve got is an ASCII 2D dungeon crawler you can only play once per day, like logging into your favorite BBS and playing LotRD. Works great on Steamdeck. UI has correct labels already applied.

A game you can't binge, you can only delve into the perilous dungeons once per day! It's really fun and the dungeon generation is more interesting than your usual "boxes and hallways". Well worth checking out if you love traditional dungeon crawlers but wished you could play on your couch as it works fantastically with a controller. Note: I did hit an issue inputting my characters name. For some reason the game didn't like the Steam virtual keyboard. I worked around this by rebinding my select key to the character I wanted to type over and over again. You could also create your character on a computer with a keyboard first. This was on Fedora 43 running Cinnamon X11

I can see myself playing this game for a long time. The design and writing are excellent with tons of humor. And the concept of only being able to do one quick run per day is very appealing to me, since I don't have much time to play but I enjoy thinking about strategies for the next day. The dungeon bested me today, but tomorrow I'll emerge victorious.
7 days, 7 delves, the game keeps pulling me back. I don't know the true depths of the game yet, but I am drawn to try and find them.

This is a great game that you start daily and delve one or more dungeons/caves, sell the loot, improve your gear and start over again tomorrow. Since you can only play one cave/dungeon instance once per day, there is no fear of missing out if you dont constantly play. All players get the same daily caves, which allows players to cooperate and discuss the caves outside the game. The controls are good, controller works great and it is easy to move around in the world and caves. It is a turn based game so you have the time to ponder your next move if neccessary. The game has a delightful light humour, which reminds me of Lucas Art games from ancient times. There are daily three different caves with increasing difficulty that changes every day, that you can explore. Once you explore a cave, you can't access that cave again until the next day. The difficulty between the caves are good, One can't simply play the hard cave instance without the proper know-how and tools. This is a game that you play in "short" sessions (depending on how much you want to do) but you will keep playing it for the long run. It is not a sprint, it is a marathon and I highly recommend it.

A lovely combination of genres and systems. It is classic Rogue with some useful modernisation, a bit of cheeky worldbuilding, and a brilliant "daily dungeon" hook. I'm playing daily and expect I will be for a long time to come.
Love the game. It is the perfect fit for me. The art is great and the humour is subtle. Cannot wait to jump in again tomorrow.
Fun trad roguelike with a twist. You can only enter the dungeon once per day. It's a nice, quick diversion from games that suck up too much time.
The daily dungeon and extraction elements add a lot of excitement to a quick, simple roguelike. A good time!

Since I discovered this game, I was so so so excited by its design and to play it with my friends. The concept feels really unique; one delve, one day. I was so hooked, I immediately created a second character after my first day and had to stop myself from being a cheesing perfectionist. The gameplay was easy to pick up and I'm enjoying learning more about the world and crafting. I've only done two delves so far, but even this morning I was extremely tempted to make an attempt before work (it's a good thing I didn't!!!). 10/10 game and it's even more fun comparing side by side with friends! Thank you for this gem! Could my character look any cooler though... each option is goofy, fun, but not quite cute c: heh
it's okay to run away
yeah that's the good stuff

As someone who wasted hours on Nethack in college (argh, last century now!), this is a delightful update of the central conceit, but with the brilliant twist of only allowing you to go dungeon delving once a day (well, technically, more than that because you can go into different dungeons if you are willing to pay) so you are limited in how much time you can actually play. There are a lot of opaque elements in both the UI and the structure - this is not a bad thing, I want to stress - and the push-your-luck feels reasonably well balanced. I expect to be revisiting this one daily for some time to come.
Perfect once-a-day dungeon crawler in the old rogue style (with a nice topping of humor added on!). Definite recommend.

Addictive little "extraction" roguelike. You get one dungeon per character per day. The dungeons are the same for all characters (don't know if they're the same for players on other computers) so you can sort of cheese it a bit by sending down some canaries to scope out the good loot, but they still need to be able to survive. The once a day mechanic means the smaller dungeon sizes still feel fun to play, you're balancing your health and light against your desire to hit the bottom of the dungeon and find all the loot you can - die and you lose nearly everything you were carrying. Great fun to jump in for half an hour or so each day and there is plenty of progression to be had so it will be a while before you exhaust all the content.
Very barebones. It feels like the one play per day limit is only there so it takes longer for you to realize it's so shallow.

A cute retro roguelike with a town to explore and things to learn along the way. I really like the (kinda) one dungeon per day feel to it, and the use of DOS text mode graphics. Also death isn't permanent...

Dungeons of Freeport is really brilliant; I fell in love with the graphics shown in the trailer (the UI and the town just looked really cute, and that a lot of heart went into both) and was rewarded with the actual game matching my expectations: the town is very cute, I love how the signs pop up with cute little graphics, I love how you can interact with all the townspeople and see them go about their routines, I love how there are just a bunch of extraneous details; and the gameplay too: it plays very well on a controller (my hands are fried for keyboards), has a very streamlined roguelike experience that feels like a mix of classic rogue with the junk-loot of extraction games, and the dungeons often (so far) boil down to: "getting into melee range likely means you just die in one hit without OK items, so use ranged combat until you run out of ammo and then either scram or risk melee"; the 1/run day is satisfying even if a delve gets completely botched. The only complaint is that I'm starting to feel, fairly early on, that I might be scratching the limits of content currently; I still haven't bought my house, though, but it mostly seems that the bestiary isn't too big nor the full list of items/gear too interesting (I don't think there are any magick artefacts or things like that; but maybe) -- so my hope/wish as a fan and lover of Dungeons of Freeport are just for some expansions to the item list, bestiary, and perhaps a bit more life for the town of Freeport itself. Otherwise a huge fan, look forward to my delve every day.
A fun little bite sized trad roguelike. There's exploration, persistent upgrades between sessions, and rudimentary crafting. A good coffee break game.
Old-school dungeon crawler with turn-based combat. Explore, loot, fight. Classic RPG feel.
Feels like an old dungeon crawler somebody infused with tavern chaos and tabletop nonsense. Messy, charming and surprisingly addictive in co-op.
This game is actually a roguelike! (though has meta)
Made here in Sydney!
